report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. Strong clinical trial evidence and medical guidelines confirm that exemestane significantly reduces the incidence of invasive breast cancer in postmenopausal women at elevated risk.

### Evidence Summary

1. **Clinical Trial Data (MAP.3 Trial):** 
   In the landmark randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 MAP.3 trial, daily exemestane reduced the relative risk of invasive breast cancer by 65% in high-risk postmenopausal women over a median follow-up of 3 years (https://www.hmpgloballearningnetwork.com/site/frmc/articles/exemestane-reduces-breast-cancer-risk-postmenopausal-women; https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/Nejmoa1103507).

2. **Professional & Regulatory Guidelines:** 
   - The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recommends offering risk-reducing medications, including aromatase inhibitors such as exemestane, to women at increased risk of breast cancer who are at low risk for adverse drug effects (https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/breast-cancer-medications-for-risk-reduction).
   - Results presented through the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) support exemestane as an effective preventative option to substantially lower breast cancer incidence among postmenopausal women with elevated risk factors (https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/research/exemestane-reduces-risk).
